config.title: How to Spend a Sunday in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Quick answers on what is open, where to go, and how a Berlin Sunday actually works.

items.q: Are shops open on Sunday in Berlin?
items.a: No. Germany's shop-closing law keeps normal shops, supermarkets and chemists shut all day on Sundays and public holidays. The exceptions are supermarkets inside big train stations like Hauptbahnhof and Ostbahnhof, corner shops called Spätis, restaurants and cafés, pharmacies on rotating emergency duty, and museums and attractions. Regular shops only open on the two designated shopping Sundays the city grants each year, which for 2026 fall on 6 December and 20 December, usually from 1pm to 8pm.

items.q: What is there to do in Berlin on a Sunday?
items.a: Sunday is Berlin's best day if you stop looking for shops. Start at a flea market such as Mauerpark, Boxhagener Platz or Arkonaplatz, have brunch or coffee nearby, then either visit a museum if the weather is grey or head to a park, canal or lake if it is not. In the late afternoon, Mauerpark with its free Bearpit Karaoke is the classic Berlin-Sunday finish.

items.q: What time do Berlin flea markets open on Sunday?
items.a: The Flohmarkt am Mauerpark runs from around 9am to 6pm. Boxhagener Platz in Friedrichshain is open Sundays from 10am to 6pm, and Arkonaplatz in Prenzlauer Berg runs year-round. The Nowkoelln Flowmarkt on the Maybachufer canal in Neukölln is only on the first and third Sunday of the month, roughly April to November, from 10am to 5pm. Go early for the best finds, or around midday for the atmosphere, and bring cash.

items.q: Is Bearpit Karaoke at Mauerpark on every Sunday?
items.a: Almost, in season. Bearpit Karaoke runs most Sundays from about May to October, starting around 3pm, but only when it is not raining, and it stops for winter. It is free, held in the little stone amphitheatre in Mauerpark, and packed with people cheering on whoever sings. Check the Bearpit Karaoke website before you make a special trip, because rain cancels it.

items.q: Are museums open on Sunday in Berlin?
items.a: Yes. Most Berlin museums, including the Museum Island museums, run their normal Sunday hours, so a Sunday is a great museum day. The day to watch out for is Monday, when many museums close. The one big exception on Museum Island is the Pergamon Museum, which is shut for a long renovation. Because Sunday is popular, book timed tickets for the big names online the night before to skip the queue.

items.q: Where can I buy food if the shops are closed on Sunday?
items.a: You have plenty of options even though supermarkets are shut. The supermarkets inside major train stations such as Hauptbahnhof, Ostbahnhof and Friedrichstraße stay open on Sundays, corner shops called Spätis sell drinks and snacks, and restaurants, bakeries and cafés are open as normal. Sunday brunch is a Berlin ritual. Just buy any picnic supplies before you settle into a park, because there is no full supermarket run until Monday.

items.q: Does Berlin public transport run on Sundays?
items.a: Yes. The U-Bahn, S-Bahn, trams and buses all run a normal Sunday timetable, and with no commuter rush it is one of the easiest days to get around. Two things to know: the U-Bahn only runs through the night on Friday and Saturday, so on a Sunday night you should check your last train, and the ferries count as normal public transport on your ticket, which makes them a nice cheap Sunday ride.
